newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa sees moderate 97 European air cargo.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa sees moderate 97 European air cargo.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG sees only moderate growth for its European air cargo business in 1997, Joachim Haas, the airline's senior vice president Europe, said.
The Deutsche Lufthansa all-freight airline saw European sales revenue rise three to four percent in 1996 compared to the previous year, he told Reuters in an interview.
"We expect a small growth in 1997 of about three percent. We think moderate growth is realistic but we have no reason to be euphoric," he said.
Haas declined to give an absolute figure for Lufthansa Cargo's European turnover but noted that inner-European income comprised about 25 percent of the total Europe revenue.
Lufthansa Cargo had a load factor of more than 80 percent in its Europe region, mostly comprising its ex-Frankfurt intercontinental flights, he said.
This was less than the near-90 percent achieved in 1995, which was a boom year, but similar to the normal 1994 levels, Haas pointed out.
He said the airline maintained its share of a difficult Germany market last year but gave no other details of market shares.
Outbound flights had a higher load factor than return legs due to higher growth in European exports compared to imports, Haas noted.
On February 10, the German airports association (ADV) said the country air cargo exports grew 6.5 percent in 1996 to 1,011,904 tonnes with imports gaining 5.1 percent to 919,382 tonnes.
Imports to Europe from Japan, for example, would probably fall again this year as Japanese firms switched to foreign production sites, he added.
The main goods shipped by air cargo in 1997 would continue to be automotive products, chemical and pharmaceuticals and computer and entertainment electronics.
"There are enormous growth rates in automotive products," Haas noted.
But demand from producers of semi-conductors was also increasing rapidly due to new production locations around the world, he added.
In imports, perishable goods including flowers and vegetables still played a major role. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax +5017
